text: Epithelium [Gr. epi + qhlh , a nipple or papilla]: Ger. Epithel ; Fr. épithélium ; Ital. epitelio . Cellular covering of free surfaces of the body and of all natural cavities which open, either temporarily or permanently, to the exterior; also applied to lining of serous, lymphatic, and vascular channels and cavities which do not open to the exterior. Cf. ENDOTHELIUM. The term was originally used of the mucous membrane of the lips and mouth, where the etymological significance of the word is plain. ( C.F.H. )
